combos.name: Eight hits a turn
combos.how: The Genji Glove lets Locke hold a weapon in each hand, and the Master's Scroll makes Fight hit four times at half damage, so each turn lands eight hits, each capped at 9,999. Both weapons ignore defense.
combos.note: The two weapons peak at opposite ends. The Ultima Weapon is strongest at full HP (and weaker below level 64); the Valiant Knife adds Locke's missing HP to every hit, so it's strongest when he's hurt. Either way one of them carries the turn.

combos.name: Dice from the back row
combos.how: Fixed Dice damage comes from the roll and Setzer's level (the three dice multiplied, times 2, times his level, and multiplied again on triples), not from his Strength. The Master's Scroll throws them four times a turn.
combos.note: Put Setzer in the back row: the dice aren't weakened there, and he takes less damage from physical attacks.

combos.name: Five spells in one turn
combos.how: With the Soul of Thamasa every Magic turn casts two spells, and the Celestriad makes every spell cost 1 MP, Quick included (normally 99).
combos.note: First turn: one damage spell, then Quick. Quick gives two turns in a row, and each casts two more damage spells, so five damage spells land before anyone else moves. Both relic slots are used, so there's no room for Earrings.

combos.name: Jump, again and again
combos.how: The Dragoon Boots turn Fight into Jump, and the Dragon Horn makes each Jump land several times instead of once.
combos.note: The Dragoon Boots are sold in Thamasa in the World of Balance; the Dragon Horn is in Phoenix Cave or dropped by a Great Dragon.

combos.name: Both of Umaro's attacks
combos.how: Umaro picks his own actions. The Berserker Ring gives him a Throw that ignores defense, and the Blizzard Orb gives him Snowstorm, an Ice attack on every enemy; with both he can do either.
combos.note: Together they also make him absorb Fire and Ice and nullify Lightning. The Berserker Ring is in the Cave on the Veldt and the Blizzard Orb in the Ancient Castle, both in the World of Ruin.

combos.who: Sabin, or anyone who mixes Fight and Magic
combos.how: The Hero's Ring adds 25% to physical and magic damage, and its magic part stacks with an Earring, for +25% physical and +50% magic.
combos.note: For Sabin's Blitzes this beats any other pair: Raging Fist and Meteor Strike are physical, Aura Cannon and Rising Phoenix are magic. Pure casters do as well with two Earrings, and a Gigas Glove doesn't stack with the Hero's Ring.

results.name: Joker's Death
results.effect: Kills every enemy, ignoring Death immunity. Strago can learn Lv. 5 Death from it.
results.note: The rarest result: the game only allows it about 10 times in 255. Some battles never let the reels stop on 7-7-7 (listed below).

results.name: Mega Flare
results.effect: Bahamut appears and hits all enemies with non-elemental damage. Damage isn't split between targets.

results.name: Prismatic Flash
results.effect: Non-elemental damage to all enemies. Always available, so it's the most reliable strong result.

results.name: Chocobo Stampede
results.effect: Non-elemental damage to all enemies, ignoring Defense. Damage isn't split between targets. Misses flying enemies.

results.name: Summon
results.effect: Summons a random Esper, except Odin, Raiden and the four GBA-only Espers.

results.name: Mysidian Rabbit
results.effect: What you get from any losing spin. Restores a little HP to the party and cures Darkness, Poison and Sleep. Doesn't hurt undead allies.

results.name: Joker's Death (party)
results.effect: Kills your whole party, ignoring Death immunity. A full party KO is a Game Over.
results.note: Watch the third reel when the first two land on 7.

when.note: The opening march through Narshe and its mines, until the armor is lost. Terra has all eight abilities; Vicks and Wedge have the three beams and Healing Force.
After Doma is poisoned, Sabin and Cyan steal Magitek Armor to escape the camp. They only have the three beams and Healing Force.
The party rides Magitek Armor through one section of the dream caves. Terra gets all eight abilities if she's in the party; everyone else gets the three beams and Healing Force.

characters.name: Terra
characters.join: Game opening, Narshe. She leaves after the battle at Narshe until you find her in Zozo. World of Ruin: Mobliz.
characters.play: High Magic, average elsewhere. Wears heavy armor and most swords and daggers. Learns magic on her own as she levels.
characters.skill: Trance: for a short time she deals double physical and magic damage and takes half damage from magic. The gauge fills as she earns Magic AP after battles.

characters.name: Locke
characters.join: Narshe, when he escorts Terra out. World of Ruin: Phoenix Cave.
characters.play: High Speed, decent Strength, low Magic. Light armor and shields only, but every dagger and some of the best swords.

characters.name: Edgar
characters.join: Figaro Castle, early in the World of Balance. World of Ruin: Nikeah and the sunken Figaro Castle.
characters.play: Very good Strength, average elsewhere. Spears, swords, every shield and heavy armor.

characters.name: Sabin
characters.join: Mt. Kolts (Imperial camp). World of Ruin: Tzen.
characters.play: High Strength, Speed and Stamina, low Magic. Claws, light armor and light shields.

characters.name: Cyan
characters.join: Doma Castle, in Sabin's scenario. World of Ruin: Mt. Zozo.
characters.play: Solid Strength with katanas and most heavy armor; weaker elsewhere.

characters.name: Shadow
characters.join: South Figaro, hired in Sabin's scenario; he may leave between battles. World of Ruin: Colosseum (bet the Striker), only if you waited for him on the Floating Continent.
characters.play: High Speed and Strength. Daggers, ninja blades, light armor and shields. His dog Interceptor sometimes blocks attacks and counters.

characters.name: Gau
characters.join: The Veldt, in Sabin's scenario: feed him Dried Meat. World of Ruin: the Veldt.
characters.play: Strong all-round stats, high Strength and Speed. Can't fight normally or use weapons (except the Impartisan); can wear the Snow Scarf.

characters.name: Celes
characters.join: South Figaro, in Locke's scenario. World of Ruin: Solitary Island (she starts the second half).
characters.play: Good all-round stats and high Magic. Strong swords and heavy armor. Learns magic on her own as she levels.
characters.skill: Runic: holds her sword ready and absorbs the next spell cast by anyone, cancelling it and turning its MP cost into MP for her. Needs a sword that allows Runic.

characters.name: Setzer
characters.join: Jidoor opera house, after he kidnaps "Maria". World of Ruin: Kohlingen café, then Darill's Tomb for the Falcon.
characters.play: Balanced stats, nearly every light and heavy armor, and unique card and dice weapons with no back-row penalty.

characters.name: Strago
characters.join: Thamasa. World of Ruin: Fanatics' Tower (Cult of Kefka), with Relm in the party.
characters.play: Above-average Magic, weak elsewhere. Rods, a few daggers and robes.

characters.name: Relm
characters.join: Thamasa. World of Ruin: Jidoor (Owzer's mansion).
characters.play: Highest base Magic and good Speed, but low Strength and Stamina. Daggers, brushes, robes and costumes.

characters.name: Mog
characters.join: Narshe moogle cave (briefly in Terra's scenario); joins for good at Narshe in the World of Balance. World of Ruin: Narshe cliffs (choose Mog over the Gold Hairpin).
characters.play: Above-average Magic and Speed. Spears, daggers, light armor and shields; can wear the Snow Scarf.

characters.name: Gogo
characters.join: World of Ruin only: Triangle Island; let a Zone Eater swallow the party.
characters.play: Below-average stats and can't equip Espers, so only HP and MP grow. Daggers, rods and light armor.
characters.skill: Mimic copies the last action anyone in the party took, free of MP and items. Gogo's other three commands can be set to almost any party command (Steal, Blitz, Tools, Lore and more) from the Status screen.

characters.name: Umaro
characters.join: World of Ruin only: Umaro's Cave north of Narshe, with Mog in the party.
characters.play: Huge Strength and Defense. Can't equip anything but relics, use Espers, magic or items.
characters.skill: Always berserk: attacks or tackles on his own. Relics add moves: the Berserker Ring lets him throw a party member, the Blizzard Orb adds an ice storm.

s: Raft down the Lethe River with Banon. The raft stops at two forks and asks which way to go. After Ultros, the party splits into three scenarios you can play in any order. This guide plays Sabin's first, then Terra's, then Locke's.
b: Play Sabin's scenario first. Gau joins on the Veldt in Sabin's scenario, and the Veldt runs through every group of enemies you've met, one battle per group. Playing Terra's and Locke's scenarios first adds about three groups (roughly 15 become 18), so every Rage takes about 20% longer to show up. That matters most for {m:Guard Leader} (Wind Slash), the best Rage you can get this early: it's one of eight battles in its group, so expect around 120 Veldt battles. Terra's and Locke's enemies add no top-pick Rages; pick theirs up on the optional Veldt trip in 1.20.

There's no treasure on the river; the forks only change how many fights you get.
Fork 1: Straight, Left or Right. All three meet again at a small cave with a save point. Left is the shortest, with a few fights at most and sometimes none. Straight is the longest, with the most fights and the best chance to meet a {m:Lesser Lopros}. Right is in between.
Fork 2: Up or Left, after the save point. Up is a loop: a run of fights that brings you back to this same fork, so you can ride it again to grind. Left goes on to a second cave with a save point, then a short stretch to Ultros.
boss: Weak to Fire and Lightning. Terra's Fire, Sabin's Aura Cannon and Edgar's Auto Crossbow do the work; Banon's Health heals the party.

The Veldt goes through its groups of enemies in turn, one battle per group, so most of these turn up within 20 to 40 battles. {m:Guard Leader} is the slow one: it's one of eight battles in its group, so expect around 120. {m:Bomb}s come up every few battles.

walk.t: Sabin's Scenario: Crescent Mountain and Serpent Trench
s: Gau leads you over Crescent Mountain, south-east of Mobliz. On the ridge, Gau finds a Potion and later the diving helmet.
Dive into the Serpent Trench and ride the currents to Nikeah, then take the ferry to South Figaro.
b:
There are two forks, and you can't swim back up after picking.
Fork 1. Left: two fights. Right: one fight, then a small cave with an X-Potion chest. The two routes meet again.
Fork 2. Left: two more fights. Right: one fight, then a cave with a {e:Green Beret}. Step on the floor switch to drain the water and carry on.
Right both times gets both treasures with the fewest fights. Left both times means more battles, for EXP and more chances to meet each enemy.

Every route meets the group with an {m:Aspiran} at least once, so Gau's Gigavolt Rage (a top pick) is safe either way. Aspiran answers any damage that isn't a plain Attack with Gigavolt one time in three, which can kill a character. Hit it with Attack, or Rage as {m:Belmodar} or {m:Spritzer} to absorb Lightning.

{m:Anguiform} uses the strong Aqua Breath when it's alone, so kill a group of them together. Aura Cannon, Rising Phoenix and Thundara (from the {m:Cloud} or {m:Ghost} Rage) work well. {m:Actinian} is harmless.
An Elixir is hidden in the clock of Nikeah's inn. Buy two Silk Robes and some Smoke Bombs while you're there.

s: Escape through South Figaro Cave with Celes.

The north-east chest now holds a {e:Thunder Rod}. Celes can use it as an item to cast Thundara, which shreds Tunnel Armor. The catch: no {e:Hero's Ring} from that chest in the World of Ruin.
Leave it closed. Thunder Rods are sold in Thamasa later and can be stolen from {m:Wizard}s, and Tunnel Armor is easy enough without one: Celes's Runic absorbs its spells. Hero's Rings are scarce: Dragon's Neck (1.21), this chest, the Jidoor auction (50,000 Gil), the Zone Eater and Kefka's Tower. More come only from betting a {e:Guard Bracelet} at the Colosseum, and those are rare too.
A Hero's Ring adds 25% to physical and magic damage. The magic part stacks with Earrings; the physical part doesn't stack with a {e:Gigas Glove} or a second ring. Casters do as well with two {e:Earring}s, so the ring is for fighters who do both, like Sabin: Hero's Ring + Earring gives him +25% physical and +50% magic for his Blitzes.

s: Terra was seen flying west. Split the team: some stay to guard Narshe, the rest go after her.
Ride Figaro Castle (talk to the man in the room left of the entrance) under the desert to the western continent and Kohlingen.
b: Optional: a Veldt trip for Gau. Before going west, you can take Gau back to the Veldt for the Rages from enemies met since the first trip (listed below), including the {m:Aspiran}'s Gigavolt, a top pick. The route: Figaro Cave to South Figaro, then over Mt. Kolts to the Returners' Hideout. Take the hidden passage in Banon's room to the raft; this time the river carries you down Sabin's route. Walk through the Phantom Forest and jump down Baren Falls (no fights in either now) to reach the Veldt. Leap until you're happy, then dive through the Serpent Trench to Nikeah and take the ferry back to South Figaro.
Figaro Castle sells two new Tools for Edgar: Flash (hits all enemies) and Drill (strong single-target). Put Edgar in front for a discount.

Why Aspiran's Rage: Gigavolt does big Lightning damage, though it sometimes hits only one enemy. It pays off in Vector and the Magitek Research Facility (1.28–1.34), where {m:Sergeant}s, {m:Proto Armor}, {m:Mega Armor}, {m:Belzecue}, {m:Onion Knight}s, {m:Trapper}s and the {m:Crane (Right)} are weak to Lightning, and against {m:Ultros} at the Opera House (1.25) and Esper Mountain (1.43). It's no use against Ifrit and Shiva (1.31): both nullify Lightning.

The tube left of it goes back to the Pinwheel room, and the far left one goes outside. Next: a chest with a {e:Force Shield}, then walk around the conveyors for {e:Force Armor}. Of the two doors, the left one reaches Party 1's blocked room. Take the {e:Ribbon} there and press the floor button. The other door leads to the Gold Dragon.
Party 1 again. With the button pressed, go through the tube room (the Stoneblade chest here is always empty) to a room with {m:Fiend Dragon}s. Switch to Party 3.
boss: Optional. Cast Float, and have Celes or Gogo ready with Runic. Steal a {e:Crystal Orb} or rare {e:Blood Sword}.
It charges for a turn, then casts Thundaga on everyone. If anyone has Reflect, it bounces Thunder spells back. Thunder Shields absorb it. Drops a {e:Crystal Orb}.

chests.n: Along right side path (group 3)
In left chest on balcony (reached via double paths, group 3)
In right chest on balcony (reached via double paths, group 3)
In chest near entrance stairs (group 3)
In chest in hidden bottom room (group 3)
In right chest in bottom middle area (after MagiTek factory, group 3)
In chest on winding path (after MagiTek research facility, group 1)
In left chest in bottom middle area (after MagiTek factory, group 3)

s: Party 3 takes the last route, beats Inferno and Skull Dragon, and opens the way for the others.
b: Party 3. Ride the left conveyor down. Take the door on the left through a passage to a metal ramp with two chests: a {e:Gauntlet} (left) and a {e:Nutkin Suit} (right). {m:InnoSent} and {m:Gamma} are tough here. Go back and take the other door into a Magitek factory room, which has a {e:Hero's Ring} and a hidden {e:Aegis Shield}.

Aegis Shield path, in the dark to the left of the spinning machine: all the way down, all the way right, all the way down, 1 step up, all the way left, all the way down, then a few steps right to the chest. Go back into the dark, all the way right, then up and right until you stop, then all the way left and all the way up to come out.

Out of the factory, take the tube to the left, past a save point. Seven steps on, Inferno attacks. After it, a passage of {m:Landworm}s: a Megalixir chest is on the right. On the left, an open chest with a red sparkle is a switch: touch it to extend Party 1's broken conveyor. Ride the conveyor to the {e:Rainbow Brush} (Relm), then take the door to the Skull Dragon.

Past Skull Dragon, Party 3 reaches the grand hall. Stand on a button while Party 2 stands on the other to open the big door. Party 1 can now cross its extended conveyor ({e:Pinwheel} chest on the left) to the raised walkway. All three parties now meet on the walkway.
boss: A surprise fight. Weak to Lightning. {m:Rahu} (left blade) only attacks physically; {m:Ketu} (right) also uses Metal Cutter. Destroy the blades or focus the body.
Weak to Fire and Holy. Drops a {e:Muscle Belt}.

chests.n: In hidden chest south of Poltrgeist statue, two steps right from entrance and straight down

s: Rearrange the parties on the raised walkway using three floor buttons and a falling weight, then fight the Guardian.
b: Put your strongest party in the middle, the average one on the right and the weakest on the left. Each path ends at a statue: the middle path has the Guardian and then Demon, the right path has Goddess, and the left path has Fiend.

How to swap: Party 1 goes through the door and walks left; the path closes behind it. Party 2 does the same, mirrored. Party 3 stands on the last button and a path forms. Switch to whichever party needs to step off a button.
After the Guardian, a save point appears. Further on, at a garbage tunnel exit, a {e:Ribbon} is hidden south of the door: go down to the wall, 2 steps right and 1 down.
boss: It hits hard with magic. Cast Reraise, and use Thundaga, Phantom Rush, Jump and Bahamut. Steal a {e:Ribbon} or the rare {e:Force Armor}.

s: Each party fights one statue goddess. Beat all three to reach Kefka.
b: {e:Thunder Shield}s absorb or nullify Wind and Wave Cannon and halve Fire, which helps in all three fights.
boss: Middle path. The easiest of the three: she's vulnerable to Stop. Stop her, then Shell up and attack. Dispel Stop from your own characters right away; she finishes them with Blaster. Drops a {e:Radiant Lance}.
Right path. Steal a {e:Minerva Bustier}; drops {e:Excalibur}.
Left path. Weak to Holy. Steal a {e:Safety Bit}.

s: Before the fight, pick a party order. The first four go in. When a tier ends, anyone who is KO'd, Petrified or a Zombie is swapped out for the next person on your list.

The fight climbs three tiers of the statue of the gods, then Kefka himself. HP, MP and status effects carry over between tiers. Rages, Dances, Runic stance and the Golem or Fenrir summon effects don't.
Tier 1: Visage, Long Arm and Short Arm. Tier 2: Tiger, Machine, Magic and Power. Tier 3: Lady and Rest. Then Kefka.
b: Steal on the way up. Lady carries the {e:Ragnarok} sword and Rest carries the {e:Ultima Weapon}. Every tier 1 and tier 2 enemy has an Elixir, and Kefka has a Megalixir. Bring Locke (or Gogo with Steal) wearing the {e:Thief's Bracer}; these enemies are level 58 to 74, so the success chance is low without it.

Tier 1 is the easiest, so use it to set up: Hastega, Mighty Guard (or Protect and Shell), Regen and Reraise. They carry into the next tiers. Save Golem or Fenrir for tier 3, where Rest's dying attack can remove a character for good.

Air Anchor (Edgar) and Death spells work on some tier enemies and save a lot of time. None of the tier enemies can be Sketched, Controlled, Scanned or Metamorphed, and Strago can't learn Lores in this battle.

Farm them after the credits. Save when the game asks after the ending. On that clear save you can fight the final battle again, and each time steal another {e:Ragnarok} and {e:Ultima Weapon} and keep them. Bet the Ragnaroks at the {c:Colosseum} for Lightbringers.
Terra can Morph in tier 1 and let the timer run out while she's asleep. That makes her Morph last for the rest of the fight.
boss: Tier 1. Kill it first with an instant-death attack: Air Anchor, or Break until it lands.
Tier 1. Mostly physical attacks. Cast Slow on it, then deal with Visage before finishing it.
Tier 1. Weak to Fire: single-target Firaga or thrown Flametongues. Once it's below about 10,000 HP it petrifies with Dread Gaze, so kill it before Short Arm.
Tier 2. Kill it first with Air Anchor or a Death spell.
Tier 2. Casts a stream of strong spells. Silence it (or use Bad Breath), then deal with it after Tiger.
Tier 2. Only attacks physically; Slow it and leave it for last. Its death throes are ten weak hits.
Tier 2. The real threat once it's hurt: it attacks every turn and can Zombie with Zombie Fang. Weak to Ice: Blizzaga and thrown Icebrands. Cure Zombie right away.
Tier 3. Kill her first, or she revives Rest. Use non-elemental, single-target attacks: Drill, Flare, Fixed Dice, thrown shuriken. Steal the {e:Ragnarok} first.

Tier 3. Steal the {e:Ultima Weapon}. Below about 10,000 HP it casts Meteor every turn, so push through that stretch fast. When it dies it uses Repose, which removes a character for good, so keep Golem or Fenrir up.

Opens with Heartless Angel (everyone to 1 HP), so heal right away. Later he charges up Forsaken, then counters attacks with Hyperdrive and, below 10,240 HP, Ultima. Attack mostly while he's charging Forsaken, when he doesn't counter. Celes's Runic absorbs Hyperdrive and Ultima. Keep reviving: Havoc Wing does most of the killing.

s: After you beat Kefka and load your clear save, the Dragons' Den opens. It's one long GBA-only dungeon, harder than Kefka's Tower, and you split into three parties of four just like the tower.
Stock up before going in: you can return to the Falcon from the entrance to save and heal, but stores are far away.
b: Bring 99 Phoenix Downs, 20+ Tents and Ethers. For Shadow, a stack of Fuma Shuriken and Flame, Water and Lightning Scrolls.
Relics matter most: aim for four each of {e:Ribbon}, {e:Reflect Ring}, {e:Prayer Beads} and {e:Angel Wings}. All but the Ribbon are sold in shops.
A solid defensive setup carries every fight here: Protect, Shell, Fenrir's or Golem's summon, and Prayer Beads.

walk.t: Seals of Ice, Wind and Earth
s: Party 1 enters and fights Ice Dragon (Redux). Each Redux dragon breaks one kind of seal somewhere in the Den, opening new paths.
Swap parties as the routes open: Storm Dragon (Redux) breaks the Seal of Wind and Earth Dragon (Redux) the Seal of Earth.
b: {m:Zurvan} reflects your spells and answers with Reflect ???; Silence or a Death spell takes it out cleanly. Kill {m:Vilia} first; she counters attacks with Overture and confuses with Entice.
Rewards: Ice Dragon gives the {e:Final Trump} (Setzer), Storm Dragon the {e:Longinus} (Edgar) and Earth Dragon the {e:Godhand} (Sabin).
boss: It splits into four identical copies. Each one you kill fires a final Ice attack at its killer, and the survivors get more aggressive. {e:Ice Shield}s absorb its Ice attacks; hit back with Fire.
Very high evasion and speed. Use {e:Thunder Shield}s against its Wind attacks, Hastega, and attacks that don't miss: Jump, Bushido, Blitzes and Throw. Spells like Thundaga often miss.
No longer floats, and hits very hard with Earth attacks. Float the whole party ({e:Angel Wings}) and attack with Wind and Water.
walk.tr: Bone Wrist, Celestriad, Crystal Orb, Dueling Mask, Elixir x3, Force Armor, Genji Glove, Hi-Ether, Magicite Shard, Magus Robe, Megalixir, Phoenix Down, Remedy, Rename Card, Ribbon x2, Stardust Rod, Teleport Stone, X-Ether, X-Potion x2

s: Leave Party 1 on the button near the Shrine of Serenity; it holds a door open while another party explores.
Climb the stairs freed by the Seal of Wind into the Dragon Temple. Call the turtle at the water to cross, press the skull button, then fight Blue Dragon (Redux) in the middle room.
The Seal of Water breaks in the Burning Labyrinth, leading to Red Dragon (Redux).
b: Rewards: Blue Dragon gives {e:Save the Queen} (Celes) and Red Dragon the {e:Apocalypse} (Terra).
boss: The easiest of the eight. Water attacks are absorbed by Imp gear, and its Rippler steals your Protect, Shell and Haste, so skip those buffs and cast Slow and Bio on it instead. A Ribbon blocks Rippler.

You can't damage it. Just survive: it gives up its life after a set number of turns and casts two parting Fire spells. Bring Fire protection (Flame Shields, Reflect for its spells), heal constantly and keep Life 3 or Reraise up.

walk.t: Cloister of Trials and the Seal of Darkness
s: Take Party 3 into the Inner Eye Labyrinth. Push the 4-ton weight, then search between the two lava pools to unlock the Holy Dragon's room for later.
Back in the Grand Cavern, cross the long land bridges past the green-clad pushers. Get knocked off and you land in the Cloister of Trials, a room of mini-bosses.
At the end, Skull Dragon (Redux) breaks the Seal of Darkness and opens a stairway that skips the bridges.
b: An invisible chest near the weight holds an X-Potion. On the bridges, take the side path down to a chest with the {e:Celestriad}.

Cloister of Trials: {m:Earth Eater} counters with a one-hit-kill punch; cast Vanish or summon Phantom. {m:Malboro Menace} splits when killed; Banish removes it. Then pick {m:Dark Behemoth} (easier with Banish) or {m:Abyss Worm}. Falling again brings them all back.
boss: Normal damage can't kill it. Drain its 14,000 MP with Rasp (or Osmose) until it falls. Wear Ribbons against Zombie, and {e:Safety Bit}s or {e:Memento Ring}s against Lv. 5 Death.

s: Pick a party with strong group attacks and Reraise. Go to the north end of the Inner Eye Labyrinth, where the Seal of Darkness used to be, into the Holy Palace.
b: {m:Shield Dragon}s here inflict Zombie and Confuse. Silence and Stop shut them down. They sometimes drop {e:Force Armor}.
A chest in the top-left corner holds the {e:Magus Robe} (Gogo). Holy Dragon gives the {e:Zanmato}, Cyan's best katana.
boss: The hardest of the eight. It fires up to three Saintly Beams a turn and heals about 6,000 HP with Curaga when hit. Max out Magic Defense (Force Shields), wear {e:Minerva Bustier}s to halve Holy damage, keep Shell up with {s:Zona Seeker}, and Reflect the dragon to stop its healing.

walk.t: Seal of Lightning and the Treasure Room
s: Re-enter the Dragon Temple from the right entrance and ride the turtle across. Arrange the four tombstones to spell THE KING OF DRAGONS.
Gold Dragon (Redux), the last of the eight, waits at the end of the hall. Beating it breaks the Seals of Lightning, opening the treasure room and the way to Kaiser Dragon.
b: Gold Dragon gives the {e:Zwill Crossblade} (Locke). In the treasure room: three chests hold a {e:Crystal Orb}, a {e:Genji Glove} and the {m:Flan Princess} (beat it for the {e:Oborozuki}, Shadow's best weapon). The {e:Stardust Rod} (Strago) sits unguarded in the bottom-left corner.
Monster-in-a-box fights here: {m:Plague} gives the {e:Angel Brush} (Relm), and Neslug gives the {e:Gungnir} (Mog). Wear Ribbons for the Plague and Flan Princess fights.
boss: It absorbs magic like Celes's Runic, so most spells (including Cure and Haste) do nothing. Flood, Quake, Meteor and summons still work, and it's weak to Water, so Flood is your best spell. Use items to heal and Golem against its Confuse.

s: Kaiser Dragon, the Lord of Dragons, waits beyond the broken Seals of Lightning.
b: Beating Kaiser Dragon gives you the last Esper, {s:Diabolos}.
boss: It changes elemental weakness four times, refilling its HP each time, so damage only counts in its last phase. Watch which attacks it uses to tell its current element. In the last phase, attack hard and survive its final Ultima: keep Reraise and Shell up.

s: Omega Weapon, the Lord of Weapons.
boss: Bring Ribbons and heal constantly. Steal a Megalixir; it drops a {e:Murakumo}.

best.why: Easy win, and the Rename Card is the next link in a chain: bet it again for Miracle Shoes.
best.how: Setzer with plain Dice, no relics. His Dice beat the Cactuar on his first turn.

best.why: Turns a cheap item into a random Esper summon.
best.how: Same as above: Setzer with Dice wins every time.

best.why: A strong sword that uses MP for critical hits. It can break when it lands a hit, except on a Black Belt counter, so it suits Celes or Edgar swinging only in self-defense.
best.how: Sabin with two Burning Fists and a Ribbon. If Great Malboro sneezes you out you keep the Flametongue.

best.why: Cyan's better katana, and the first step of the katana chain.
best.how: Sabin with two Venom Claws and a Black Belt. Save first; it's over in a couple of turns either way.

best.why: Doubles the wearer's EXP.
best.how: Dark Force is weak to instant death. Setzer with Viper Darts (two with a Genji Glove) or a Soul Sabre.

best.why: Jump lands 2 to 4 times. One of the best relics for a Dragoon (Edgar, Mog or anyone with Dragoon Boots).
best.how: Same fight as the Organyx: Sabin with two Burning Fists and a Ribbon. If you picked the Gold Hairpin over Mog, this is the trade to make.

best.why: Only if you have a spare Ribbon. Lets you then trade the Gold Hairpin for a Dragon Horn.
best.how: Dark Force: instant-death weapons, as for the Growth Egg.

best.why: The best armor for Terra, Celes and Relm: absorbs Fire, Ice, Lightning and Wind, halves the rest, and adds 25% MP.
best.how: Equip a Reflect Ring and just run. Death Machine casts Death, which bounces back and kills it. Don't attack: hurting it triggers up to four Blaster counters. The Regal Gown is in Daryl's Tomb.

best.why: Permanent Safe, Shell, Haste and Regen.
best.how: Fiend Dragon. Dragoon Edgar with a Flame Shield. Fallen One drops you to 1 HP, so it's a gamble, but it's the payoff of the Elixir chain.

best.why: Stronger katana for Cyan.
best.how: Gorgimera. Dragoon Edgar with a Flame Shield, which blocks its Surge and Flare Star. An Ice Shield doubles Aero damage, so don't use one.

best.why: The best lance for Edgar or Mog: Holy element, +3 Magic, and casts Holy one time in four.
best.how: Galypdes. Instant death doesn't work; send Dragoon Edgar and hope.

best.why: Absorbs Fire, nullifies Ice. Bet it again for an Ice Shield.
best.how: Outsider is weak to instant death: Setzer with two Viper Darts and a Black Belt.

best.why: Absorbs Ice, nullifies Fire, +10% magic block. Bet it back for another Flame Shield to get a set of each.
best.how: Metal Hitman has little HP. Sabin with two Dragon Claws and a Black Belt.

best.why: The strongest throwing star for Shadow, and hard to get anywhere else.
best.how: Chaos Dragon can kill in one hit. Dragoon Edgar and hope; expect to retry.

best.why: Sabin's best armor; nullifies Fire.
best.how: Test Rider. Wear an Ice Shield to absorb its Flash Rain.

best.why: Great armor for Mog and Gau, and the start of the Ward Bangle chain. Behemoth Suits come from the Veldt.
best.how: Outsider: Setzer with two Viper Darts and a Black Belt.

best.why: Recruits Shadow, if he survived the Floating Continent. He shows up as the opponent and joins you whether you win, lose or Teleport out.
best.how: Win or lose, Shadow joins.

best.why: A relic that heals HP as you walk.
best.how: Siegfried's Hyperdrive kills in one hit. Shadow with the Kagenui (random Stop), Dragoon Boots, Dragon Horn and high magic block.

best.why: Relm's best rod.
best.how: Tonberry counters any damage with Cleaver plus Traveler, so you must kill it in one hit. Protect against Break (Reflect Ring, Ribbon, Safety Bit), raise HP (Muscle Belt, Red Cap) and use a Master's Scroll with Fixed Dice or the Valiant Knife.

best.why: Lets anyone equip any weapon or armor.
best.how: Slagworm is weak to instant death. Wear Angel Wings (against Quake) and a Thunder Shield (against Sand Storm). Mog with 255 Defense can't lose.

best.why: Fewer random battles. Handy for the Dragons' Den.
best.how: Yojimbo. Max magic block (Force Shield, Force Armor, Priest's Miter, White Cape) on Setzer with Fixed Dice and a Master's Scroll.

best.why: A second Dragon Horn.
best.how: Yojimbo again, same setup.
Aspidochelon is easy: weak to Holy, low HP. Sabin with two Dragon Claws, a Black Belt and Gaia Gear.

best.why: A strong armor from a suit few can wear.
best.how: Aspidochelon, as above.

best.why: Steal becomes Mug (attack and steal in one turn).
best.how: Amduscias. 255 Defense and a Ribbon or Peace Ring against its Confuse.

best.why: Turn spare Genji Gloves into Thunder Shields, which absorb Lightning and are very useful in Kefka's Tower.
best.how: Demon Knight. Equip a Reflect Ring to bounce its Holy.

best.why: Same idea with spare Gauntlets.
best.how: Vector Chimera. Thunder Shield plus Red Jacket blocks all its strong attacks; Edgar works well.

best.why: The Lightbringer is a stronger sword than the Ragnarok. Each time you fight the final battle you can steal another Ragnarok from Lady, so you can turn every one into a Lightbringer for Terra, Celes and Locke.
best.how: Daedalus.

best.why: A GBA-only relic. Bet it again for a Dragon Horn.
best.how: Behemoth King.

best.why: Another Dragon Horn.
best.how: Vector Chimera. Thunder Shield plus Red Jacket.
Tonberry, as for the Magus Rod.
